guidelines.fragment_description: A class is a blueprint for objects, encapsulating attributes and operations relevant to the model domain.
An association represents a relationship between two classes, depicting how instances of each class are related.
An aggregation is a special form of association representing a whole-part relationship where the part can exist independently of the whole.
A composition indicates a strong whole-part relationship between classes where the part cannot exist independently of the whole.
A generalization connects a subclass with a superclass, representing an inheritance relationship where the subclass inherits attributes and operations of the superclass.
A dependency shows that a change in the supplier class may affect the client class, indicating a usage relationship.
An attribute is a named property of a class that provides information about the class instances.
An operation is a function or a service that can be performed by an object of the class.
